The trailer for Michael B. Jordan’sThe Thomas Crown Affairremake remake is out, and it looks to be as sexy, heisty, and suave as the 1999 Brosnan/Russo version. The Oscar winning actor directs as well as stars, with Adria Arjona and Kenneth Branagh along for the ride.

The new extended trailer for the first wave ofPokopiaDLC gives us a much better look at all the water type monsters you’ll be able to befriend in Bubbly Basin beginning August 5th. It also looks likebuilding underwater housesis about to getmucheasier.

A newGoogle Workspace updatelets Gemini summarize and respond to comments, like highlighting all the unresolved changes in a document,Android Authorityreports. You can also ask Google’s AI to draft new comments and replies and add suggested edits based on comments.

Your next takeout could arrive via drone, after DoorDash announced it was launching DoorDash Air.

Bitchat, the peer-to-peer encrypted messaging app that sends messages over Bluetooth LE, can now itself be sent from one Android device to another — no internet or Google Play Store required. This is a big deal, considering India’s recent attempts toban the appfrom Github. If this isn’t cypherpunk, I don’t know what is.

New details reveal OpenAI’s agent hacked several other companies, intensifying already heightened concerns over advanced AI safety.

Apple says the “restricted mode” that9to5Macuncoveredin iOS 27 beta codewon’t be usedfor missed lease payments in the newApple Upgrade scheme. That does leave some pretty big questions about why Apple reportedly coded it in the first place though.

wtfjohnson:

So they just built this feature into the OS for funsies? 👀

In the ongoing battle for control of the messaging platform that claims over 1 billion active users, Durov has beencharged withfacilitating terrorism by failing to remove information “actively used by Ukrainian special services, terrorist organizations and extremist organizations to prepare and coordinate sabotage and terrorist acts, mass killings and cyber fraud activities” in Russia, according to theNew York Times. Durov responded like Durov.

Katalyst saysthe Link spacecraft it launched on July 3rd topush the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatoryback up to a higher orbit has been in a “multi-axis spin” over the last 72 hours, resulting in sporadic communications. Having identified the cause, Katalyst is working to recover the mission and believes Link still has “a viable path to rendezvous with Swift.”

[NASA Science]

XAI hasfiled a lawsuitin response toalaw taking effect on Saturday thatbans appsand websites from generatingnon-consensual sexualized imagery. The Musk-led company responsible for the Grok chatbot said the law will impact free speech and visual expression “in a clumsy attempt to prohibit ‘nudification.’”

“See you in court, creep,” responded Minnesota GovernorTim Walz.

Poor SK Hynix. Despite the memory-chip maker posting record net profit of about $64.64 billion, the stock fell by as much as 18 percent (down 9 percent at market close) when its revenue haul (also a record) failed to meet the lofty expectations set by the AI hype cycle. The results won’t help investorsworried that the AI bubble’s about to pop.

[WSJ]

The ultra-long rangeAirbus A350-1000ULRoperated by Qantas took off from Melbourne, Australia and flew for24 hours and 24 minutes, covering 23,075km (14,338 miles) before landing at the plane’s factory in Toulouse, France. The new aircraft will debut on the carrier’s nonstop Sydney-London route starting in 2027. ​

“We don’t have the same problems,” Logitech’s new gaming boss Robin Piispanen tells meduring ourwide-ranging chat, when I ask if PC builders are delaying peripheral purchaseslike other parts of their builddue to RAM prices. In fact, Logitech’s gaming sales are up 12 percent YoY and 21 percent sequentiallyin today’s Q1 earnings.

But other chips might leave a dent:

in late June 2026, a serious incident in the manufacturing facilities of one of Logitech’s semiconductor suppliers resulted in its temporary closure, which is likely to impact the Company’s ability to effectively meet future demand. The Company is working on multiple mitigation plans.

“Only the survival of our studio would ever make us consider such a painful action,” Double Fine founder Tim Schafersays in a statement. “Our transition to becoming an independent company also means becoming a size that we can sustain.”

Double Fine was one of four studiosXbox sold offas part of its recent restructuring, and the studio gets tokeep its games.

The statement follows a recent high-profile cybersecurity incident that rocked the AI industry.

You can play the game now if you’re willing to wait through launch queues, which don’t currently seemtoobad. For more onEQL, check outmy retrospectiveand Kallie’sinterview with the developers.

Light CEO Kaiwei Tang explains why Light made a flip phone, how the world’s opinion of smartphones is changing, and whether you can cure your tech problemswith more tech.

Zuckerbergargues thatbringing “superintelligence” to more people is better than centralizing who controls AI:

As intelligence becomes abundant, the most important question will be how we direct it. Some argue that superintelligence itself, or a small set of experts who control it, should decide what is best for humanity. I disagree. The history of democracy and economics has shown that there is no single objective answer to how people define the best life, and therefore the best approach is letting people decide what matters to them.
